JAKA introduces Kargo50 and Zu50 for heavier factory work

The wheeled platform targets tote handling; the separate Zu50 arm carries 50 kilograms.

Pandaily ↗11 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Two approaches to factory handling

JAKA announced the wheeled Kargo50 humanoid and Zu50 collaborative arm for an October 12 CIIF debut in Shanghai. Kargo50 targets tote and material transfer, while Zu50 extends the company’s higher-payload arm range.

Keep model specifications separate

Pandaily cites a 50-kilogram payload and 2,100-millimetre reach for Zu50, but no verified Kargo50 payload specification. A claimed improvement from 105 to 28 seconds per tote belongs to the earlier Kargo10 and must not be attributed to the new model.

Demonstrations versus deployment results

A factory-style booth pairs wheeled robots for engine transport and screw tightening, with JAKA EVO linking task planning to motion control. Demonstrations and manufacturer claims still require validation for each customer’s speed, durability and cost requirements.
